thread.title: Apple shares fall as holiday sales forecast misses estimates -

author: Bloomberg News
title: Apple shares fall as holiday sales forecast misses estimates -
text:
Apple Inc. gave an underwhelming forecast for the key holiday period suggesting weaker-than-expected demand for the company’s pricier new iPhones.
The Cupertino, California-based technology giant expects fiscal first-quarter 2019 revenue to be between US$89 billion and US$93 billion. Analysts were looking for US$92.7 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.
Apple shares fell more than 4 per cent in extended trading on Tuesday. The stock closed at US$222.22 in New York, leaving it up 31 per cent this year. Apple suppliers declined after the report.
Apple Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook cited weakness in some emerging markets, currency volatility, the timing of new iPhones and uncertainty about whether Apple can meet demand for all the new models it recently released, according to an interview with Reuters.
IPhone unit sales barely grew from a year earlier, even though new flagship iPhones came out in the fiscal fourth quarter this year. That was a disappointment, considering there were no big iPhone launches in the same period last year.

The iPhone’s average selling price was $793 in Apple Inc.’s fiscal fourth quarter. The company sold 46.9 million iPhones in the quarter, generating revenue of US$37.2 billion. The period included about a week and a half of sales of the high-end iPhone XS and iPhone XS Max models. The average iPhone selling price was US$793. Analysts were looking for 48.4 million iPhone units in the quarter, and an average selling price of US$729.
The company released new iPhones in September, and upgraded iPads and Macs were introduced earlier this week. Apple raised prices on most of the devices, a relatively recent strategy to offset slowing unit sales growth. It’s a bet that consumers will continue to pay up for access to the company’s specialized and tightly integrated hardware and software.
The iPhone XR is one of the few outliers from the trend of more costly Apple gadgets. With a starting price of US$749, it’s expected to be a popular holiday gift, luring owners of older iPhones to upgrade. The iPhone still looms large over Apple’s fortunes, accounting for more than 60 per cent of revenues. It’s also the central hub for connecting the other devices and using services.
Fiscal fourth-quarter sales rose 20 per cent to US$62.9 billion, Apple said. Profit came in at US$2.91 a share. Analysts expected revenue of US$61.4 billion and earnings of US$2.78 a share.
